Hypertrophy was enhanced by higher volume (>=10 sets/muscle group/week, dose-response) and eccentric-only vs concentric-only contractions; it was not affected by frequency (1 vs >5 days/week, volume equated), load (30-100% 1RM), failure, repetition speed (0.5 vs 8 s), periodisation or exercise order; evidence was insufficient for rest interval, range of motion, set structure, machine vs free weight and single- vs multi-joint. The text cites a meta-regression showing diminishing returns beyond ~2-3 sets per exercise for strength and ~18-20 weekly sets for hypertrophy and advises at least two sets per exercise; it states progression is needed for continued long-term gains and that periodisation is not superior to non-periodised progressive training. Certainty was expressed as quality-of-evidence percentages, not GRADE.
references.limitations: Overview of reviews inherits the biases and overlap of included reviews; evidence searched to Oct 2024 so excludes Pelland 2025; labelled consensus where it goes beyond data.
references.gradeReason: Consensus position stand built on a systematic overview of 137 reviews of RCTs; indirect, aggregated evidence.
